deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::1 Roles and parties
front: In the US, Canada and Mexico, who prepares and transmits the customs declaration, using our data?
back: A **licensed customs broker**: CBP-licensed in the US, CBSA-licensed in Canada, and in Mexico an agente aduanal (or agencia aduanal).
extra: The broker files, but the data is ours: classification, value and origin come from our master data. If our data is wrong, the filing is wrong, even though a licensed broker sent it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::1 Roles and parties
front: Who is legally responsible for a US entry's accuracy, duties and records, even though a broker files it?
back: The **importer of record (IOR)**. It must use reasonable care (19 U.S.C. 1484), and the duties are its personal debt to the US (19 CFR 141.1).
extra: Common mistake: thinking the broker is liable. If the broker fails to pay CBP, having paid the broker does not discharge the importer's debt. Relying blindly on the broker is not reasonable care.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::1 Roles and parties
front: Why does our team audit what brokers file, if brokers are licensed experts?
back: Because in all three countries the importer, not the broker, stays responsible for accurate declarations and duties. We supply the classification, value and origin data, so we check that the broker declared it correctly.
extra: Reasonable care in practice: we can show how each classification, value and origin was decided, and we regularly reconcile what the brokers filed against our master data.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::2 US entry lifecycle
front: After CBP releases the goods, what must the broker file within 10 working days, with the estimated duties?
back: The **entry summary** (CBP Form 7501 data), with the estimated duties deposited (19 CFR 142.12).
extra: Duty is deposited per entry, or monthly through the Periodic Monthly Statement (PMS).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::2 US entry lifecycle
front: After the entry summary, what is CBP's final computation of the duties, taxes and fees owed on a US entry?
back: **Liquidation**: it ends in a bill, a refund or no change. ACE usually schedules it about 314 days after entry; the legal limit is 1 year, extendable to 4 (19 U.S.C. 1504).
extra: Why it matters: after liquidation a Post Summary Correction is no longer possible, so changes generally need a protest. Check the scheduled date in ACE rather than assuming 314 days.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::2 US entry lifecycle
front: Within 180 days after liquidation, what can the importer file to challenge a CBP decision?
back: A **protest** (19 U.S.C. 1514), filed in ACE or on CBP Form 19. The Senior and trade counsel lead it; we supply the evidence.
extra: Order to remember: a Post Summary Correction before liquidation, a protest after it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::2 US entry lifecycle
front: Which filing corrects an error on an accepted US entry summary before liquidation?
back: A **Post Summary Correction (PSC)** in ACE: within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever comes first.
extra: Escalate errors fast: the earlier one is caught, the more correction routes are still open.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::2 US entry lifecycle
front: What is the difference between a US entry and an entry summary?
back: The **entry** (CBP Form 3461 data) asks CBP to release the goods. The **entry summary** (CBP Form 7501 data) declares classification, value and origin and deposits estimated duties. They can be filed together.
extra: Memory hook: the entry gets the goods out of the port; the entry summary does the accounting.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::3 Duties and fees
front: PART-A: 2,000 kg, entered value US$8,000. What duty does a compound rate of 2% + $0.10/kg give?
back: **$360**: 2% × $8,000 = $160, plus $0.10 × 2,000 kg = $200. A compound duty charges an ad valorem part and a specific part on the same tariff line.
extra: For comparison: 5% ad valorem alone gives $400, and $0.30/kg specific alone gives $600. The rates here are hypothetical: never quote real rates from memory.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::3 Duties and fees
front: An item's value doubles, but its weight and duty rates stay the same. Which type of duty does not change, and why?
back: **Specific duty**: it is charged per unit, such as per kg, so it follows quantity, not value. Ad valorem duty doubles; compound duty rises only by its ad valorem part.
extra: The flip side: a wrong quantity or unit of measure changes a specific duty even when the value is right. Unit-of-measure mismatches are a known data-quality break.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::3 Duties and fees
front: How is the US Merchandise Processing Fee (MPF) charged on formal entries and on informal entries?
back: Formal entries: a percentage of value, with a per-entry minimum and maximum. Informal entries: a small flat fee (19 CFR 24.23). CBP changes the amounts every fiscal year.
extra: Never quote MPF amounts from memory: take them from the tariff landscape doc and note the date you checked. Originating goods properly claimed under USMCA are exempt.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::3 Duties and fees
front: Which US imports pay the Harbor Maintenance Fee (HMF)?
back: Commercial cargo unloaded from vessels at covered US seaports, as a percentage of value with no minimum or cap (19 CFR 24.24). Air, truck and rail shipments do not pay it, and neither do exports.
extra: For landed cost, HMF depends on the transport mode: the same item pays it when it arrives by ocean, not when it arrives by truck.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::4 Trade systems landscape
front: What does a Global Trade Management (GTM) system do?
back: It holds trade compliance master data and runs the trade processes on it, such as classification per country, origin and trade agreement qualification, and duty calculation.
extra: Today these functions are spread across the AS400 trade system, custom tools, spreadsheets, the brokers and Oracle. The e2open project moves some of them into one system.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::4 Trade systems landscape
front: Where does the AS400 trade system sit in our trade data flow?
back: Between **Oracle** and the **brokers**: items come in from Oracle, and a product file goes out to each broker, who files with customs. The AS400 data and the brokers' entry data feed **reporting**.
extra: This is the generic flow from the primer. In M2 the Manager shows our real interfaces, schedules and files.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::4 Trade systems landscape
front: Which vendor's GTM applications will replace the AS400 trade system, in a project expected to start in January 2027?
back: **e2open** Global Trade Management. You will be a core project BSA: as-is process docs, data mapping and cleansing, and UAT.
extra: Until the project confirms scope, do not assume which e2open applications, countries or interfaces we get: each is a question for the kickoff.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::4 Trade systems landscape
front: Which system is the source of the new and changed items that flow into the AS400 trade system?
back: **Oracle**, our ERP, which also holds purchase orders and standard costs. In the trade system the team adds each new item's classification and origin, with maker-checker review.
extra: What goes wrong: an item set up in Oracle but never classified leaves the broker to classify it on its own, so the first entries use a guessed code. A report of active items with no classification per import country catches it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: In a tariff action, what does Research own and what does Standard Cost own?
back: **Research (Hire A) owns the WHAT**: which items are in scope, the rates and dates, and the sources. **Standard Cost (Hire B) owns the $**: landed cost and margin, the Oracle cost update, and variance.
extra: Research hands off in the Tariff-Impact Brief, which contains no $ figures. Both work in one shared Tariff-Impact Model. A brief with $ figures, or a cost model that re-interprets scope, is sent back.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: Standard Cost thinks an item that Research's brief puts in scope is really out of scope. Who decides?
back: **Research decides scope.** Standard Cost never decides or re-interprets scope: it computes the $ on Research's determinations and raises its doubt with Research.
extra: A cost model that re-interprets legal scope breaks the boundary rule, and the checker sends it back. One owner per decision keeps the brief and the model consistent.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: Before a tariff model or standard cost update is released to the business, what review must it pass?
back: A documented **checker review** by the Senior or the Manager, recorded on the Jira ticket. The maker never approves or releases their own work.
extra: The checker records name, date, version reviewed and findings. Maker-checker continues after day 90: ownership means running the cycle as maker. Hire B never loads to Oracle production without Finance and checker sign-off.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: A live tariff action takes effect in fewer than 5 business days. Who is maker?
back: A **trainer**: the Senior for the WHAT, the Manager for the $, with the other trainer as checker. The hires shadow and draft a parallel practice brief or model, reviewed afterward.
extra: The same applies to any business-critical action, and in W1–W2 the trainer is always maker. Within 2 working days the hires write after-action notes.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: With 5 to 15 business days before a tariff action takes effect, when does the checker review the hire's draft?
back: **The same business day it is submitted.** The hire is maker, with a 15-minute daily checkpoint, and nothing is released before the checker's review.
extra: With more than 15 business days, the hire is maker on the normal cycle, and the work replaces that week's track session.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: Before your day-60 review, you have a question for a customs broker. What do you do?
back: Send it to the **Senior** (or the Manager). Before day 60 you never contact a customs broker, agente aduanal or trade counsel directly.
extra: The Senior decides whether to ask the broker. After day 60, with the Senior's agreement, you may email the broker with the Senior copied.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::5 Ground rules: maker-checker, boundary, brokers
front: Before the day-60 review, what production write access may a hire have?
back: **None.** From W6 you get edit rights on a test copy of your own tool, never on production. At the day-60 review, the Manager can grant production change rights for that one owned tool.
extra: Even then, every change goes through change control: tested in the test copy, a change request, a maker-checker review and the Manager's release approval. No other production write access in the first 90 days.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: Under the recommended model, which connections may use the team's service account?
back: Only **saved, unattended connections**: Power BI gateway data-source credentials, Power Automate connections and scheduled jobs on the server. **Nobody** signs in with it interactively, and hires never see its password.
extra: It has the same access as the whole team, so anyone signing in with it could do all of that without leaving their own name. Its password lives in the password vault, held by the Manager (or IT). The Manager confirms the final model before access requests go out.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: A colleague offers you their login 'because it's quicker'. Why do you refuse, and what do you ask for instead?
back: Because **every action must be traceable to the person who did it**: maker-checker only works if the record shows who made what. Say no, ask them to **share their screen**, and tell the Manager the same day.
extra: The same goes for the service account password. If you saw or heard a password, say so, so it can be changed; never write it down. A leaver's personal account is simply disabled, but a shared password stays known until someone changes it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: On Oracle EBS production, DBeaver asks you to confirm a statement before running it. What does that tell you, and what do you do?
back: The statement would **change data**, and EBS production is **read-only** for you. Answer **No**: you write only small, filtered, row-limited SELECT queries, never DML or DDL.
extra: DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE) changes data; DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) changes structure. Your personal EBS account is read-only at the database, confirmed by the Manager: that is the real control, and DBeaver's settings are a safety net. If something already ran, stop and tell the Manager within the hour.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: In the team database, where may you create and load tables, and how do its other tables, views, procedures and jobs change?
back: Only **your own tables in the sandbox** schema, dropped when you are done. Everything else is **use only**: you never create, alter or drop objects there; they change **through the Senior**.
extra: Nothing a report, flow, app or tool relies on may ever read from a sandbox table. Outside the sandbox: no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or 'Edit Top 200 Rows'. If your owned tool needs a change to team-database objects, it goes through a change request with the Senior as checker.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: You want Copilot to explain an old Python script for your tool doc, but the script holds a database password. What do you do?
back: **Don't paste the script, and don't copy or use the password.** Tell the Manager the same day: a credential in code is itself a finding. Passwords, keys and connection strings with passwords never belong in scripts, flows, files or prompts.
extra: Flag it in the tool doc's open questions. Tool code may go into Copilot only if the AI policy allows it, and only after you remove credentials, connection strings, server names and file paths.
source: Data platform primer §1.1 rule 7, §3.5 / Copilot guide §2.2

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: You want Copilot Chat's help analyzing real item costs and supplier prices. What is the rule, and what is the safest alternative?
back: Company business data needs the **Manager's OK first**, and then only the smallest piece that does the job. Safest: a **fictional copy** with the same columns, or a description of the table's shape.
extra: Never paste credentials or personal data. Public official text (Federal Register notices, CSMS messages, HTSUS notes) and fictional data are fine. The company's AI policy overrides these defaults. If you pasted something you should not have, tell the Manager straight away.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: Copilot Chat gives you an HTS code and a duty rate, with a citation. What may go into a Tariff-Impact Brief?
back: Only what you confirm in the **official source you open yourself**, cited to that source. Copilot is never the source of a regulatory fact, HTS code, rate or date: its citations are leads, not evidence.
extra: Copilot can invent a citation, cite a real document that says something else, or give a right-looking code that is not in the HTSUS. Its output is a draft: you are the maker, you must explain every line, and maker-checker review still applies.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: Copilot drafts a SQL query for you. What must happen before it runs on real data, and why is Oracle EBS stricter?
back: Read it line by line, **test it in the sandbox** or on practice data, and check row counts. The sandbox is SQL Server, so Oracle SQL can't be tested there: **you write any EBS query yourself**.
extra: Copilot may explain Oracle syntax or an existing reviewed query. Never paste Copilot-written SQL into a DBeaver session on EBS. A tested SELECT may then run under your personal login where the platform rules allow; anything that loads or changes data runs only in the sandbox.
source: Copilot guide §2.4 / Data platform primer §1.1 rule 11

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 01 · Week 1 · Roles, US entry basics, trade systems, safe-use rules::6 Safe use: data platform and Copilot
front: Copilot Chat answers confidently about one of our items' cost history. Why should you treat the answer as a guess?
back: The free Copilot Chat **cannot see our internal data**: not our systems (team database, EBS, AS400), files or Teams chats. Apart from Outlook, it sees our data only when you paste or upload it (as of Oct 2026).
extra: So anything that sounds company-specific is a guess. In Outlook it can see your own inbox and calendar (rolling out to users without the paid license). In Edge, asking about the open page or tabs counts as pasting them.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::1 Canada
front: What identifies a Canadian importer to the CBSA, and what is it made of?
back: The **BN15**: the 9-digit Business Number plus the import-export (RM) program account, e.g. 123456789RM0001. Both come from the Canada Revenue Agency; the importer then registers in the CARM Client Portal.
extra: It is the Canadian counterpart of the US IOR number and Mexico's RFC, and AMPS penalties are issued against it. Importer identifiers are set up once; changes are rare and risky.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::1 Canada
front: To get release prior to payment (RPP) in Canada, what must the importer post in CARM?
back: **Its own financial security.** Since the CARM transition ended on 20 May 2025, a broker's security no longer covers the importer. Without its own security, duties and taxes are payable at release.
extra: RPP is what lets goods be released first and paid later, through the monthly statement of account in CARM.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::1 Canada
front: Under CARM, which declaration replaced the B3 to account for a commercial import's duties and taxes?
back: The **Commercial Accounting Declaration (CAD)**, since 21 October 2024. Corrections and adjustments are submitted as new versions of the CAD.
extra: It does the job of the US entry summary: classification, value for duty, origin, tariff treatment (for example CUSMA), duties and GST. CARM has been the system of record for these since the same date.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::1 Canada
front: After an RPP release in Canada, how long does the importer have to get the CAD accepted?
back: **5 business days** after release; the release day is day 0. The duties and GST then post to the monthly statement of account in CARM.
extra: Compare the US: the entry summary is due within 10 working days of release. Late accounting in Canada can draw an AMPS penalty against the importer's BN15, some issued automatically.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::1 Canada
front: You find today that a filed Canadian CAD declared the wrong origin. What must happen, and by when?
back: The importer must correct the declaration and pay any duties owing within **90 days** of forming reason to believe it is wrong (Customs Act s. 32.2). Escalate to the Senior the same day.
extra: The clock starts when we form reason to believe, not at import. It covers origin, tariff classification and value for duty. Before the day-60 review you do not contact the broker; the Senior decides the correction route.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::2 Mexico
front: Besides an active RFC, which SAT registry must a Mexican importer be registered in before it can import?
back: The **padrón de importadores**, plus a padrón sectorial for certain listed goods. Registration requires an active RFC, a valid e.firma and tax compliance.
extra: The importer also authorizes its agente aduanal electronically (the encargo conferido). All of these must be in place before the agente files the first pedimento.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::2 Mexico
front: For each Mexican import, which declaration does the agente aduanal prepare, validate and transmit?
back: The **pedimento**: one declaration with classification (fracción + NICO), value, origin, regime and taxes. Its key shows the regime, e.g. A1 = definitive import.
extra: Mexico has no separate release filing and accounting declaration: the pedimento does both jobs. The importer stays responsible for what it declares, even though the agente files it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::2 Mexico
front: How does the timing of duty and tax payment differ between a Canadian RPP import and a Mexican import?
back:
**Canada (RPP):** release first; the CAD follows and is paid on the monthly statement.
**Mexico:** taxes are paid on the pedimento **before** the goods are presented; then automated selection decides release or inspection.
extra: Remember: Canada = release, then account and pay. Mexico = pay, then release. A pedimento error found later is fixed by a rectificación (Ley Aduanera art. 89).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::2 Mexico
front: KIT-100 enters Mexico: valor en aduana US$20,000, IGI 10%, IVA 16% (illustrative rates, no DTA). How much IVA is due?
extra: Common mistake: IVA on the valor en aduana alone (3,200, which is 320 short). In real life DTA and other charges also go into the IVA base. IVA is generally creditable, so it usually stays out of item cost; confirm the treatment with Finance.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::3 Classification (HS, HTS, GRIs)
front: What does the 8-digit level of a US HTS number determine?
back: It is the **rate line** (the legal tariff line): the duty rate is set at 8 digits. Digits 9–10 are a statistical suffix used for trade statistics.
extra: Canada and Mexico work the same way: the 8-digit tariff item or fracción sets the rate, then 2 more digits follow (a statistical suffix in Canada, the NICO in Mexico).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::3 Classification (HS, HTS, GRIs)
front: Which part of an item's tariff code should normally match in the US, Canada and Mexico, and why?
back: The **first 6 digits** (the HS subheading), which are harmonized internationally. Digits 7–10 are national, so each country's code is classified and maintained separately.
extra: A 6-digit mismatch between countries for the same item is a data-quality flag that needs a documented reason. Log it for the Senior's review; do not change master data yourself.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::3 Classification (HS, HTS, GRIs)
front: In what order are the six General Rules of Interpretation applied, and when do you stop?
back: In numerical order, starting with GRI 1. Stop at the first rule that settles the classification; most goods are settled at GRI 1. GRI 6 applies the same logic to subheadings.
extra: The GRIs are legal rules, not guidance. In the US, also read the Additional U.S. Rules of Interpretation in the HTSUS (for example on principal use and on parts).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::3 Classification (HS, HTS, GRIs)
front: Under GRI 1, what decides a good's heading?
back: The **terms of the headings and any relevant section or chapter notes**. Section and chapter titles are for reference only.
extra: Read the notes for every candidate heading before choosing: exclusion notes often end the analysis. Move past GRI 1 only when it does not settle the case.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::3 Classification (HS, HTS, GRIs)
front: When goods fit two or more headings, how does GRI 3 decide between them?
back: In order: (a) the **most specific** description; (b) the material or component that gives **essential character**; (c) the heading that comes **last in numerical order**.
extra: 3(b) also covers retail sets: a hairdressing set (clipper, comb, scissors, brush, towel) is classified as the hair clipper. Reaching 3(c) is rare and a sign to look for a ruling.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::3 Classification (HS, HTS, GRIs)
front: Which three conditions must a kit meet to be a 'set put up for retail sale' under GRI 3(b)?
back:
1. At least two different articles classifiable in different headings.
2. Put together for a particular need or activity.
3. Packed for sale directly to users without repacking.
extra: If it qualifies, it is one article, classified by its essential-character component (GRI 3(b)), on one declaration line. If not, each item is classified and declared separately. The choice also changes how USMCA origin is tested.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::4 USMCA basics
front: What is USMCA called in Canada and in Mexico, and when did it replace NAFTA?
back: **CUSMA** in Canada and **T-MEC** in Mexico; it is one agreement. It entered into force on **1 July 2020**, replacing NAFTA.
extra: Expect all three names: Canadian tariff treatments say CUSMA, Mexican documents say T-MEC. The joint review and any changes to the agreement are time-sensitive: check the tariff landscape doc.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::4 USMCA basics
front: Who claims USMCA preference on an import, and what must they hold when they make the claim?
back: The **importer** claims it, based on a valid **certification of origin** it holds when it makes the claim. Without a claim, the good does not get the preferential rate.
extra: In the US the claim is SPI 'S' on the entry summary line; Canada and Mexico claim it on the CAD or the pedimento. Keep the certification and the BOM or supplier evidence behind it on file before claiming.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::4 USMCA basics
front: KIT-100 is assembled in Mexico from parts made in Country X. Why can it be 'of Mexico' for US marking yet fail USMCA?
back: Each purpose has its own origin test. US marking of goods from Mexico uses the 19 CFR Part 102 tariff-shift rules; USMCA preference uses the Annex 4-B product-specific rule. Passing one proves nothing about the other.
extra: A country-specific additional duty uses yet another test: usually substantial transformation, unless the action's legal text says otherwise. Never reuse one origin answer for another purpose.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::4 USMCA basics
front: Why does a wrong HS classification put a USMCA preference claim at risk?
back: The product-specific rule is looked up by the good's HS code, and a tariff shift compares the codes of the good and its non-originating materials. A wrong code tests the claim against the wrong rule.
extra: It can also hide a valid claim. When an item's code changes, re-check its USMCA qualification (Customs primer §8.4, step 7).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::5 Trade data flow
front: After filing, what do the brokers send back to us, and what is it used for?
back: **Line-level entry data**: US entry summary, Canadian CAD and Mexican pedimento lines. It is the actual duty for PPV, the basis for broker audits and the import side of drawback.
extra: The importer can also pull its own declaration data from the ACE Portal (US) and the CARM Client Portal (Canada): useful to cross-check what the brokers send.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::5 Trade data flow
front: An AS400 screen lets you change trade data, although your access should be inquiry-only. What do you do?
back: **Stop and tell the Manager.** Use only display options: your AS400 access is meant to be inquiry-only, whatever a screen allows.
extra: Never run a menu option or job you do not fully understand, such as anything that sends files to brokers or updates rates. Prefer warehouse copies and extracts to production.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::5 Trade data flow
front: On a typical AS400 trade system, what builds each broker's product file and sends it?
back: A **scheduled batch job**, often nightly. Its failures are usually silent: if it does not run, the broker files with yesterday's codes.
extra: For each job that matters to your process, find out what it does, when it runs, who is alerted when it fails, how it is rerun and who owns it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::5 Trade data flow
front: How does the receiving side prove that a product file or an entry data file arrived complete?
back: From its **control record**: a header or trailer with the record count and totals, compared with what was actually loaded.
extra: Every interface also needs a reject file with an owner, someone who checks that it ran, and a test file before any layout change.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::5 Trade data flow
front: What must happen to each loaded line of the brokers' entry data before it can feed audits and PPV by item?
back: It must be **matched to one of our items**. Track the match rate and work the unmatched lines in an exception queue.
extra: Each line is matched to an item and also to its PO or receipt line (Trade systems primer §2.2).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: How does Oracle EBS data get into the team database, and what does that mean for how fresh a Power BI report is?
back: As a **scheduled copy**: the team database is as fresh as its last successful load. A report is no newer than its last refresh, and that refresh is no newer than the last load.
extra: Every hop is a copy with a schedule, so ask 'as of when?' before you quote a number. EBS is the most current source but the most expensive to query: look in the team database first.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: Which component lets Power BI, Power Automate and Power Apps reach the on-premises team database?
back: The **on-premises data gateway** (standard mode). Every Power BI refresh, flow and app on the team database passes through it, so when it is offline they all fail at once.
extra: Gateway admins manage it and its connections; you only report failures. A personal-mode gateway serves one user and Power BI only, so team solutions should use the standard one. Triage clue: many things failing from the same moment, or a restart of the server it runs on.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: Two people with different database rights open the same Power BI report. Whose credentials did its refresh through the gateway use?
back: Neither person's: every refresh through the gateway uses the connection's **one stored credential**, not the viewer's (unless single sign-on is set up). Under the recommended model that is the **service account**.
extra: Connection users can use a gateway connection but cannot see or change its credentials. Whoever's credentials sit in a connection is who the data source sees, so the platform map records each connection's account, never its password.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: Which Power BI item holds the data, relationships and measures, is what refreshes, and can feed many reports at once?
back: The **semantic model** (formerly 'dataset'). Because many reports can share one model, a change to the model, or to the view it reads, reaches every report built on it.
extra: A report is only the pages and visuals on top. When a number is wrong, first decide which one you are looking at: wrong data or logic in the model, or a wrong filter on the report page.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: In a Power BI workspace, what can a Contributor do that a Viewer cannot, and which role do you hold on production before day 60?
back: A **Contributor** can create, edit and delete content and schedule refreshes; a **Viewer** can only view and interact with it. On production workspaces you are a **Viewer**; Contributor only in a personal or dev workspace.
extra: Above them, a Member can also add people and publish the workspace app, and an Admin can do everything. A person in several groups gets the highest of their roles. Before day 60 you share nothing: send people the existing report link.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: A Power BI report shows last Tuesday's data. Where do you look first, and who fixes a credential error you find there?
back: The semantic model's **refresh history**: the last successful refresh and its error text, which usually names the cause. A credential error goes to the **gateway connection owner**; you never re-enter credentials yourself.
extra: Check whether other models on the same connection failed at the same time: a rotated service-account password breaks them all. A renamed or removed column goes to the Senior with the model owner. Triage is read-only: never restart or re-run anything, or edit a connection.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: The maker of a production Power Automate flow leaves the company. What breaks, and what would have prevented it?
back: Steps that use **the leaver's connections fail** until someone updates the credentials. Prevention: **co-owners**, connections under the agreed account model, and flows kept in **solutions**, with owners and connections recorded in the tool doc.
extra: A flow acts with the credentials of the connections inside it. Never 'fix' a broken production flow by signing its connection in with your own account: it would then run as you and break again when your password changes. When anyone leaves the team, the Manager runs the platform map's leaver check.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: A Power Apps app on a large SQL Server table shows fewer records than the same count in SSMS. What is a likely cause?
back: **Delegation.** When a formula cannot be delegated to SQL Server, Power Apps fetches only the first records, up to the app's data row limit, and works on those alone. Results can be silently incomplete.
extra: Power Apps marks such a formula with a delegation warning (a blue underline). Triage: write down the app, the screen, the filter and both counts, and send them to the app owner. Hire B: a cost app on a large table can hit this.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 02 · Week 2 · Canada, Mexico, classification, USMCA, data platform::6 Our data platform: how the pieces connect
front: You finish work on the shared remote server. Why do you sign out instead of just closing the Remote Desktop window?
back: Closing the window only **disconnects**: everything you started keeps running in memory. **Signing out** ends your programs and deletes your session. A forgotten session uses memory and can keep files open.
extra: A file left open in your session, such as a tool's workbook, can block a scheduled job that needs it. Disconnect only if the Manager or the tool owner asks you to keep something running; anything that must run on its own belongs in a scheduled task.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::1 Valuation
front: We provide our supplier, free of charge, a mold for making our parts. What is the mold called in valuation, and how is it treated?
back: An **assist**. Its value is added to the customs value, apportioned over the shipments made with it, although it appears on neither the invoice nor the PO.
extra: The classic BSA data gap: assists are often recorded nowhere, so a value built from purchase prices is too low. The apportionment method must be reasonable and applied consistently; the Senior agrees it with the broker.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::1 Valuation
front: How is a commission we pay our own buying agent treated in transaction value, compared with a selling commission paid by the buyer?
back: A **buying commission** is not added. A **selling commission** paid by the buyer is one of the five additions. The same holds in the US, Canada and Mexico.
extra: Check who the agent works for: our own agent (buying) or the seller's (selling). The five additions are added only if they are not already in the price.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::1 Valuation
front: Price US$10,000 FOB. We pay freight 800, insurance 50, buying commission 200, and supplied a mold free (1,000 apportioned). Customs value in US, Canada, Mexico?
back: **US and Canada: 11,000** (price + mold assist). **Mexico: 11,850**: it also adds freight and insurance up to arrival. The buying commission is added nowhere.
extra: US and Canada are FOB-like, Mexico is CIF-like. Transaction value is the first of six valuation methods; almost all our imports should use it, and the others apply, in order, only when it cannot.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::1 Valuation
front: Our landed-cost model converts at Finance's planning exchange rate. Why will its duty differ slightly from the duty the broker files?
back: The broker converts at the rate each country fixes for a set date (US: the certified rate for the **date of exportation**). The model's planning rate differs, so a small gap is expected and should be explainable in PPV.
extra: Canada uses the Bank of Canada rate for the date of direct shipment; Mexico generally the rate for the date of entry. When model and filed duty differ slightly, check the conversion rate and date first.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::2 USMCA origin rules
front: What are the four ways a good can be USMCA-originating?
back: Origin criteria (Art. 4.2): **A** wholly obtained or produced in the region; **B** meets the product-specific rule; **C** made exclusively from originating materials; **D** a narrow case decided by an RVC test.
extra: A good with any non-originating material can only use B (or the narrow D). The criterion goes on the certification as data element 7.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::2 USMCA origin rules
front: A product-specific rule reads 'a change to heading 84.AA from any other heading'. What must be true of each non-originating material?
back: It must be classified in a **different heading** (4 digits) from the good: a tariff shift. A non-originating material already in 84.AA fails, unless de minimis covers it.
extra: Look the rule up by the finished good's HS code. A change of chapter compares 2 digits, a change of subheading 6. Read 'except from heading Y' clauses carefully. Originating materials do not need to shift.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::2 USMCA origin rules
front: Pump PK-100 (TV US$211) fails the change of heading only because its US$25 non-originating housing shares the pump's heading. What does de minimis show?
back: **25 / 211 = 11.8%**, over the 10% limit, so the tariff shift still fails. Next, test the rule's alternative: regional value content.
extra: At a housing cost of US$14 (TV US$200), 14 / 200 = 7.0%: de minimis would save the shift and the pump would qualify under criterion B. De minimis compares the failing materials with the good's transaction value or total cost (Art. 4.12).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::2 USMCA origin rules
front: Fictional rule: RVC at least 60% (transaction value) or 50% (net cost). PK-100: TV 211, net cost 185, VNM 89 (US$). Which method qualifies?
back: **Net cost:** (185 − 89) / 185 × 100 = **51.9%**, at least 50%. Transaction value gives (211 − 89) / 211 × 100 = 57.8%, under 60%, so it fails.
extra: Only the producer can calculate and support net cost, so the producer (or exporter) would normally certify. Real rules state their own methods and thresholds: read the rule, never assume one.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::2 USMCA origin rules
front: Retail set KT-200 (GRI 3(b)) is worth US$50; only its US$4 bit set is non-originating. How is its USMCA origin decided, and with what result?
back: By the **sets article** (Art. 4.17), not one product-specific rule: every good must originate, or the non-originating goods must be at most 10% of the set's value. 4 / 50 = **8%**: the set originates.
extra: If the bit set cost US$7 (set US$53): 7 / 53 = 13.2%, so the set fails unless the bit set itself originates. The article applies only when the kit is classified as a set; otherwise qualify each item separately.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::3 Certification and records
front: Who may complete a USMCA certification of origin?
back: The **importer, exporter or producer** (USMCA Art. 5.2). If qualification rests on the producer's own cost data, such as net cost, the producer (or exporter) normally certifies.
extra: Mexico has accepted importer certifications since 1 January 2024. Do not confuse the certifier (who completes it) with the claimant: the importer always makes the preference claim.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::3 Certification and records
front: What form must a USMCA certification of origin use, and what must it contain?
back: **No set form**: any format, even on the invoice, works if it contains the **nine minimum data elements** of Annex 5-A. NAFTA's CBP Form 434 is no longer used.
extra: Review each supplier certification for all nine elements, the item match, the blanket period and the signature; reject incomplete ones. Element 7, the origin criterion (A to D), must match the qualification result.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::3 Certification and records
front: How long a period can one USMCA blanket certification cover for repeat shipments of identical goods?
back: **Up to 12 months**, stated on the certification. Start the next supplier request before it ends: an expired certification leaves the claim unsupported.
extra: Supplier solicitation tracks this. Useful measures: certifications expiring in the next 60 days, and claims filed without a certification on file (should be zero).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::3 Certification and records
front: How long must an importer keep the certification, BOM and calculation behind a USMCA claim?
back: At least **5 years after importation** (USMCA Art. 5.8); **6 in Canada**. Keep the certification, BOM and calculation, supplier certifications, cost data and proof of the transaction.
extra: Do not confuse it with the 4 years for which customs must accept a certification after it is completed. US import records in general: 5 years from entry (19 CFR 163.4); drawback records until 3 years after the drawback claim is liquidated.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::3 Certification and records
front: A qualifying good entered the US without a USMCA claim. How long does the importer have to claim, and what does an approved claim refund?
back: **One year from importation**, by a post-importation claim (19 U.S.C. 1520(d)) with a certification. An approved claim refunds the excess duty **and the MPF** paid.
extra: Pub. L. 116-260 (2020) authorized the MPF refund, back to 1 July 2020; ignore older CBP guidance that says MPF is not refunded. CBP cannot extend the one-year deadline. At entry, the claim is SPI 'S' on the line.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::3 Certification and records
front: CBP sends a Form 28 request for information about a USMCA claim. What must the BSA be able to produce, and what if it can't?
back: The item's **qualification file**, within days: certification, BOM and calculation, supplier certifications and origin information. Without that support the claim can be denied, with duties, interest and possibly penalties.
extra: Tell the Senior the same day and pull the data; the Senior, not you, replies to CBP and the broker. Build the file when the claim is made: rule text, who prepared, who checked, the date.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::4 Reading a tariff action
front: A press release and a fact sheet announce a new US tariff action. Which document actually governs its dates, scope and rates?
back: The **legal instrument**: the proclamation, executive order or notice. Press releases, fact sheets, news and law-firm or broker alerts are only leads: use them to find the instrument; when they differ, the instrument wins.
extra: Fact sheets have differed from the proclamation on rates and dates. Annexes can be posted later or corrected, and one action can come as several proclamations on the same day.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::4 Reading a tariff action
front: Which CBP publication tells filers the Chapter 99 numbers and reporting order for a new US action?
back: A **CBP CSMS message** (Cargo Systems Messaging Service). Read every follow-up message too: CBP corrects details, such as drawback treatment or exemption lines, in later messages.
extra: It often comes the day before or the day of effect, sometimes before the Federal Register. Cite it in the brief with the instrument. Daily monitoring starts with the CSMS folder.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::4 Reading a tariff action
front: Where in the HTSUS does a new US additional duty get its own heading, reported on the entry line next to the normal code?
back: In **Chapter 99**, subchapter III (9903 headings). The 9903 number is reported **in addition to** the Chapter 1–97 classification, never instead of it.
extra: The 9903 number tells CBP which action, exemption or exclusion applies, and so which extra rate to charge. Some 9903 numbers mean 'not subject': reporting them claims the exemption. The HTSUS revision can lag the effective date.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::4 Reading a tariff action
front: What decides whether a new US duty applies to goods shipped before its effective date but entered after it?
back: The **entry**: goods entered for consumption (or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption) on or after the stated date and time pay it. PO, ship and receipt dates do not count, unless the action says otherwise, such as an in-transit provision.
extra: Quote the timing clause word for word, including the time and time zone (daylight or standard). Goods in a bonded warehouse take the rate in force when they are withdrawn (19 CFR 141.69).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::4 Reading a tariff action
front: In a Tariff-Impact Brief, how do you record an action's timing, scope, exclusion and stacking wording?
back: **Quote, then interpret.** Paste the exact words first. Write 'our working interpretation' separately underneath, with a confidence level: High, Medium or Low.
extra: Medium or Low items that change scope, rate or date need broker or counsel confirmation, through the Senior, before release. A brief with an open Low item goes out only as 'provisional', with the Manager's approval.
source: Tariff-Impact Brief template, How to fill this in

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::5 BSA intake and requirements
front: A requester asks which items a new tariff action hits and what it does to our cost. How is the request set up in Jira?
back: As an **epic** with two linked stories: Research (the WHAT, in a Tariff-Impact Brief) and Standard Cost (the $, in the Tariff-Impact Model). The Research story **blocks** the Standard Cost story.
extra: The boundary rule in action: Standard Cost never decides scope; it computes $ on Research's determinations. Each story has its own maker and checker.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::5 BSA intake and requirements
front: During intake triage, which conditions make a request P1?
back: Any one of: **Urgency 3 and Risk 3**; wrong data reaching a broker, Finance or a system **now**; or a regulatory effective date **within 10 working days** that may cover our items.
extra: Tell the Manager at once (within 30 minutes for a new tariff action). In days 1 to 60 the Manager confirms every P1 or P2 priority, and every decline, before you send it.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::5 BSA intake and requirements
front: How should one requirement be written, and what does an 'and' inside it usually signal?
back: As **one testable sentence**: 'The [tool, report or process] shall [behavior] [condition].' An 'and' usually means two requirements: split them.
extra: Every Must also needs acceptance criteria a tester can check with real data, often as Given/When/Then. Give each requirement a source (person and date, regulation, defect); confirm or delete any without one.
source: Requirements template, How to fill this in

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::5 BSA intake and requirements
front: In a requirements document, how does a business rule differ from a requirement? Give a duty-rate example.
back: A **business rule** is true whatever the system: a US import pays the rate in effect at entry. A **requirement** says what the system does about it: 'The tool shall store an effective-from date for each rate.'
extra: Keep them in separate sections, each with a source. Rules on scope, rates and dates come from a checked Tariff-Impact Brief; cost rules, such as the costing reference date, come from Finance policy.
source: Requirements template, How to fill this in

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: What are the four BABOK v3 requirement types, and how do they relate?
back: **Business**: why the change is made. **Stakeholder**: what each stakeholder needs to achieve it. **Solution**, functional and non-functional: what the solution must do, and how well. **Transition**: temporary, what the move to the future state needs.
extra: Writing them separately stops anyone from designing a solution before the need is agreed. Functional = a capability (behaviour and information); non-functional = a quality or condition, usually measurable, such as 'returns its result in under 2 minutes'.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: 'Purchasing needs the in-scope item list, with the reason for each item, 2 working days before the pricing meeting.' Which requirement type is this?
back: A **stakeholder requirement**: a need of a stakeholder that must be met to achieve the business requirement (knowing before the effective date which items the action covers). Solution requirements then say what the query and brief must do.
extra: Find it by asking the requester about the decision: 'Which items, by what date, and what happens if an item is missing from the list?' Give it a source, here the intake interview.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: Before e2open cutover, classification history must be migrated and reconciled to the AS400 counts. Which requirement type is this?
back: A **transition requirement**: it is needed only to move from the current state (AS400) to the future state (e2open), so it is **temporary**. Solution requirements say what e2open itself must do.
extra: You will meet them as core BSAs on the e2open project, where your work is as-is documentation, data mapping and UAT (BSA primer §1.2). The reconciliation method is in the data mapping spec, 04 Part 7.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: In BABOK, what is the difference between verifying a requirement and validating it?
back: **Verify**: it meets quality standards and is usable for its purpose (well written). **Validate**: it aligns to the business requirements and supports the needed value (the right one). A requirement can be verified and still fail validation.
extra: Common mistake: taking a well-written requirement for the right one. Verify it yourself with the nine quality checks (BSA primer §5.2) before any review; validation then asks which business requirement it serves.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: 'The report should be fast.' Which requirement quality check does it fail most clearly, and how would you rewrite it?
back: It is not **testable**: nobody can agree whether it passed. Strong: 'The report refreshes in **under 5 minutes** for **12 months of entries**.' A value and a scope give a clear pass or fail.
extra: Words like 'fast', 'recent' and 'works correctly' are the warning signs: replace each with a value, a date range or an observable result. The nine checks are those commonly listed from BABOK task 7.2, Verify Requirements.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: In MoSCoW, how do you test whether a requirement is really a Must, and what do the Musts form together?
back: Ask: **if it is not delivered, would we cancel or refuse to go live?** If not, it is not a Must. Together, the Musts are the **Minimum Usable SubseT** of the change.
extra: A workaround that holds for a while makes it a Should, not a Must. DSDM: Musts take no more than about 60% of the effort and Coulds about 20%. Coulds drop first when the date is at risk; 'Won't Have this time' is written down so it is not quietly reintroduced.
source: BSA primer §5.5; Requirements template, MoSCoW priorities

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: How is a Given/When/Then acceptance criterion built, and what must a set include when dates are involved?
back: **Given** a known starting state, **When** an action or event, **Then** an outcome someone can observe. Use concrete data (an item, an HTS number, a date) and at least one **edge case**, such as the day before an effective date.
extra: Example: 'AC2 Given an entry dated the day before the effective date, when duty is calculated, then the additional duty is not applied.' One behavior per criterion; never 'works correctly'. These criteria are what make a story pass INVEST's T (Testable).

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: In a requirements traceability matrix, what does tracing backward find, and what does tracing forward find?
back: **Backward**, to each requirement's source, finds requirements **nobody asked for**. **Forward**, to its story and acceptance criteria, test case, result and release, finds requirements **nobody built or tested**.
extra: When a requirement changes, the matrix shows what it touches: other requirements, stories, tests, data maps, the tool doc (BSA primer §5.7). For a small change, the story's acceptance criteria plus the change request's test table are the trace.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 03 · Week 3 · Valuation, USMCA origin, records, tariff actions, BSA fundamentals::6 Business systems analysis fundamentals
front: Why ask 'How do you check the HTS list before it goes out?' instead of 'You check the HTS list against the annex, right?'
back: The second is a **leading question**: it puts your answer in the other person's mouth, and people agree to be polite. The **neutral, open** question lets them describe what really happens.
extra: Open questions start a topic, probing ones get under 'usually', and 'show me' asks for the real file. Keep closed questions for confirming facts at the end. Then send a written recap: for scope, rates, dates or cost, silence is not agreement.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::1 IMMEX and Mexican programs
front: What does an IMMEX program let a company do, and which import duty does it defer?
back: Import inputs, parts and machinery **temporarily** to manufacture, transform or repair goods for export, without paying the general import duty (**IGI**) at import. The program comes from the 2006 IMMEX Decree.
extra: IMMEX = Industria Manufacturera, Maquiladora y de Servicios de Exportación. Companies that also hold SAT's IVA/IEPS certification cover the IVA and IEPS on temporary imports with a tax credit instead of cash. Who owns IMMEX compliance here: ask the Senior.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::1 IMMEX and Mexican programs
front: How long can temporarily imported IMMEX raw materials, parts and components generally stay in Mexico?
back: **Generally up to 18 months** from import (Ley Aduanera art. 108). Machinery and equipment can stay as long as the IMMEX program is in force.
extra: Verify the current text of art. 108 before using a period in real work. Our data link: the IMMEX status we send the broker makes an import temporary, so a wrong status or a missed discharge lets inputs overrun their time limit unnoticed.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::1 IMMEX and Mexican programs
front: What is the legal status of IMMEX temporary imports that are not exported or changed to another regime within their time limit?
back: They are **deemed to be in Mexico illegally**, because the temporary regime has ended. IGI, IVA/IEPS with inflation updates and surcharges, and fines can then be assessed.
extra: Repeated failures put the IMMEX program itself at risk. That is why each temporary import must be discharged by an export or a change of regime in time, and why the Anexo 24 balances matter.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::1 IMMEX and Mexican programs
front: Which RGCE annex sets the automated inventory control that tracks each IMMEX temporary import from pedimento to export?
back: **Anexo 24.** It tracks each input in, consumed and out (exported, transferred or changed regime), generally first-in, first-out. The authorities must have online access to it.
extra: The return pedimento is the evidence that discharges a temporary import. A wrong fracción or item on our side means the pedimentos and the Anexo 24 records stop matching.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::1 IMMEX and Mexican programs
front: Which SAT system tracks the IVA/IEPS credits that certified IMMEX companies take on temporary imports, and in which RGCE annex?
back: The **SCCCyG** (Sistema de Control de Cuentas de Créditos y Garantías), in **Anexo 30 (formerly Anexo 31)**. It opens a balance for each covered temporary import; exports discharge it.
extra: It was Anexo 31 before the RGCE for 2022, and the trade still says 'Anexo 31'; check the numbering in the current RGCE. Its balances must reconcile with Anexo 24: discharges from the inventory feed it, so bad inventory data breaks both.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::1 IMMEX and Mexican programs
front: Why can IMMEX goods exported to the US or Canada still owe Mexican duty on their non-originating inputs?
back: **USMCA Article 2.5** limits duty deferral programs such as IMMEX for non-originating inputs in goods exported to another USMCA country, so Mexican duty on those inputs can become payable.
extra: The same article also limits US drawback on non-originating goods exported to Canada or Mexico. How it applies to our goods is a question for the Senior: do not work it out alone.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::2 Broker audits and corrections
front: Auditing a broker's filed entry line, which four fields do you compare first, and why those?
back: **Classification, value, and origin with the preference claim**, which set the duty, plus the **duty rate and amount** filed. These four drive the money and most of the risk.
extra: Compare the classification with ours for that item, country and date: an old code is a typical mismatch. Compare value with the invoice and PO price plus additions. Then check quantity and unit of measure, the US manufacturer ID and the importer identifiers.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::2 Broker audits and corrections
front: Your audit finds a filing error. How soon must you escalate it to the Senior, and why?
back: **The same day.** In Canada the 90-day reason-to-believe clock may already have started; in the US the Post Summary Correction window may be closing.
extra: First contain it: tell the data owner and stop more filings going out with the known-bad value. Log the evidence: item, entries affected, filed and correct value, source, date found. If the Senior is out, escalate to the Manager.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::2 Broker audits and corrections
front: After escalating a filing error, what must your scope query find so the Senior can choose the correction route?
back: **Every affected entry, line and period.** The Senior or Manager then picks the route, for example a PSC, a CAD adjustment or a rectificación, with counsel where needed.
extra: You prepare the data; you never decide the route. You never contact customs, and before the day-60 review you do not contact the broker either: the Senior (or the Manager) does.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::2 Broker audits and corrections
front: An audit mismatch was caused by our own master data, not by the broker. How is the root cause fixed?
back: Raise a **change request** and fix the master data with **maker-checker review**. Correcting the filing alone leaves the next shipment wrong, because the broker files with our data.
extra: If the broker deviated from correct data we supplied, the broker owns the fix, through the Senior. Either way, the Senior decides the correction route for the entries already filed.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::2 Broker audits and corrections
front: PART-A: entered value US$40,000, broker applied 2.5%, expected rate 6.5% (fictional). What is the duty variance, and what does it mean?
back: **−US$1,600: underpaid.** Variance = entered value × (applied − expected) = 40,000 × (2.5% − 6.5%). Negative means less duty was paid than expected: log it and escalate it.
extra: Positive = overpaid, negative = underpaid. Report the two sides separately: in this table a net of −1,175 hides a 1,600 underpayment and a 425 overpayment. Do not round per line; round only the number you report.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::2 Broker audits and corrections
front: What is a US prior disclosure, and what does it do to a negligence penalty?
back: Telling CBP about a possible 19 U.S.C. 1592 violation before, or without knowledge of, a formal investigation. If the lost duties are tendered, a negligence or gross negligence penalty is limited to interest on them.
extra: Section 1592 has three culpability levels: negligence, gross negligence and fraud; for fraud, a disclosure only reduces the penalty. Hires never decide on a disclosure or estimate a penalty: escalate, and the Senior and counsel decide.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::3 Process mapping
front: What is a SIPOC, and why do you fill it in before a detailed process map?
back: A one-page process scope: **Suppliers, Inputs, Process (5 to 7 high-level steps), Outputs, Customers**. It fixes where the process starts and ends, so the interviews and the map stay on track.
extra: It takes about 20 minutes, together with the process header. Then interview the person who does the work and, separately, the person who checks it, walking through the last real instance.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::3 Process mapping
front: Which SIPOC column do you fill in first, and in which order do the other four follow?
back: **Process** first. Then work right to **Outputs** and **Customers**, then left to **Inputs** and **Suppliers**. One item per row; the rows need not line up across columns.
extra: Customers can be internal teams: in this example Standard Cost, Finance and the Manager receive the outputs. Detailed steps belong in the as-is step table, not in the SIPOC.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::3 Process mapping
front: As-is or to-be: which process do you map first, and why?
back: **The as-is first**: how the process really runs today, workarounds included. It is the baseline for requirements and gaps. Write the to-be only after the interviewee has validated the as-is.
extra: Record what really happens, not what the SOP says; a difference between the two is a finding for the pain point log. Every to-be change must link to a pain point, a requirement or a control gap.
source: Process map template, How to fill this in

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::3 Process mapping
front: When you document a maker-checker step in a process map, what must the control description say?
back: **What exactly is compared** (not just 'reviewed'), **when** it happens (before release), and **what the evidence is**, such as a Jira comment with the checker's name, date, version and findings.
extra: A person checking their own work is not a control. Mark the status Designed, Performed or Gap, and see the evidence for the last two instances before you mark it Performed.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::4 Data, SQL and Power BI
front: In a star schema, what goes in the fact table and what goes in the dimension tables?
back: **Fact:** measurable events at a stated grain, such as entry lines, with numeric measures and keys. **Dimensions:** what describes them (item, date, country, broker), with attributes to filter and group by.
extra: It is a star because each dimension joins only to the fact, never to another dimension. That keeps queries simple, and it is the shape Power BI models work best with.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::4 Data, SQL and Power BI
front: What is the grain of an entry-lines fact table, and what goes wrong if you mix grains?
back: **One row = one entry line.** Mixing grains double counts: a header-level amount such as freight, repeated on every line, is summed once per line.
extra: State the grain before you build anything. Classification has its own grain (item + country + date), so joining it without country and date multiplies rows.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::4 Data, SQL and Power BI
front: In Power BI, what cardinality and filter direction should a dimension-to-fact relationship, such as Item to EntryLines, have?
back: **One-to-many, single direction**: one item row to many entry lines, with the filter flowing from the dimension to the fact.
extra: A many-to-many prompt usually means a duplicate key or the wrong grain: fix the data first. A '(Blank)' in a slicer usually means fact rows whose key has no match in the dimension.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::4 Data, SQL and Power BI
front: Chapter 73 has two entry lines: US$20,000 with US$1,200 duty and US$40,000 with US$800 duty. What is its effective duty rate?
back: **3.33%** = SUM(duty) / SUM(value) = 2,000 / 60,000. Not 4%, the average of the two line rates (6% and 2%), which weights the small line as much as the big one.
extra: In SQL: GROUP BY LEFT(hts10, 2), then SUM(duty_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(entered_value), 0). Prove the groups add up to the clean control total, and label a missing HTS 'UNK' with COALESCE so those lines stay in.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::4 Data, SQL and Power BI
front: Why must Effective Duty Rate be a DAX measure, not a calculated column?
back: The rate must be total duty divided by total value for whatever is filtered. A per-row rate column, summed or averaged, gives wrong totals. **DIVIDE([Total Duty], [Total Entered Value])** recalculates in every filter context.
extra: Calculated column: computed per row at refresh and stored; use it for attributes you slice by. Measure: computed when queried, in the current filter context; use it for totals and ratios.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 04 · Week 4 · IMMEX, broker audits, process mapping, data::4 Data, SQL and Power BI
front: You join entry lines to a rate table and the row count goes up. What happened, and how do you fix it?
back: **Join fan-out**: the rate table has more than one row per join key, such as two effective-dated periods. Add the missing condition, e.g. entry_date BETWEEN effective_from AND effective_to, until the count equals the original.
extra: Write down the row count before and after every join or filter. In a broker audit, fan-out duplicates lines, so the duty and variance totals are inflated.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: Which regulations control most US commercial and dual-use exports, and which agency administers them?
back: The **Export Administration Regulations (EAR)**, 15 CFR Parts 730–774, administered by the Commerce Department's **Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)**.
extra: Defense articles fall under the ITAR (State Department) instead. That is unlikely for a distributor, but it must be ruled out, not assumed.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: In ECCN 3A001, what do the last three digits, 001, signal?
back: The **reason for control**. 001 is in the **0xx series: national security**. The 1xx series is missile technology and 2xx nuclear nonproliferation.
extra: Also 3xx chemical and biological weapons, 9xx anti-terrorism and other controls. Reasons can overlap: the first digit shows the one that takes precedence (0 for an item controlled for both national security and missile technology), and the entry lists every reason to check against the Country Chart.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: What designation does an item get when it is subject to the EAR but matches no entry on the Commerce Control List?
back: **EAR99**. Most everyday commercial goods are EAR99 and usually need no export license.
extra: Common mistake: 'EAR99 means no license, ever'. An EAR99 item can still need a license for an embargoed destination, a prohibited end use or a restricted party.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: Besides the item's ECCN or EAR99 status, which three facts decide whether an export needs a license?
back: The **destination** (Commerce Country Chart and embargoes), the **end user** (restricted-party lists) and the **end use** (prohibited uses). 15 CFR Part 732 sets out the steps.
extra: License determinations stay with the Senior. Your exports work is the data behind them: a wrong ECCN, destination or party record produces a wrong answer.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: What is Electronic Export Information (EEI), and what proves that it was filed?
back: Export data filed in the **Automated Export System (AES)** under the Foreign Trade Regulations (15 CFR Part 30). AES returns an **Internal Transaction Number (ITN)** as proof of filing.
extra: The USPPI, usually the US seller, is responsible for accurate EEI data; records are kept 5 years (15 CFR 30.10). An exempt shipment carries an exemption legend instead of an ITN, such as 'NOEEI 30.37(a)'.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: What is a Schedule B number, and what may an EEI filing report instead for most goods?
back: The Census Bureau's **10-digit export classification**, based on the HS. For most goods the EEI may report the **10-digit HTSUS import number** instead, unless that number is flagged invalid for export.
extra: The first 6 digits are the HS subheading, as in the HTSUS. Schedule B or ECCN data gaps in item master data are typical exports backlog items for you.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: Export to Country X, no license: PART-A $1,600 + PART-B $1,200 (same Schedule B number), KIT-300 $2,000 (another). What needs EEI, if anything?
back: **EEI is required**, but it reports only the Schedule B number of PART-A and PART-B: $1,600 + $1,200 = $2,800, over US$2,500. KIT-300's number totals $2,000, so it is exempt and left off.
extra: The test is per Schedule B number within one shipment (one USPPI, consignee and conveyance), not per line or on the shipment total: add the lines that share a number. Domestic and foreign-origin goods are tested separately. Licensed items and other mandatory cases need EEI at any value.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: Most US exports to Canada need no EEI, even above US$2,500. Which exports to Canada still need it?
back: Goods that need a **license** (and other mandatory filing cases), goods **stored in Canada** for later export elsewhere, and goods **moving through Canada** to a third country (15 CFR 30.36).
extra: Destination matters as much as value: a shipment that needs EEI to Country X is generally exempt when it goes to Canada.

deck: BSA Onboarding::Unit 05 · Weeks 5–6 · Exports, standard and landed cost, owning a tool, SDLC::1 Export compliance
front: In your first 90 days as maker on exports backlog items, which three kinds of decision stay with the Senior?
